---
title: "Skills"
---

A **skill** is a self-contained bundle — one `SKILL.md`, optional
`references/`, optional `scripts/` — that the agent loads at runtime.
The harness ships four variants under `.claude/skills/`, plus a
no-skill *baseline* that is used purely as a control for evaluation.

| Variant | Folder | Style | When to pick |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prose`   | `.claude/skills/great-tables/`         | Flowchart + full reference tree | Default. Highest polish. |
| `scripts` | `.claude/skills/great-tables-ci/`      | Flowchart + a mechanical checker loop | When you want the model to self-check. |
| `house`   | `.claude/skills/great-tables-house/`   | One worked script + short rules | Minimal cognitive load. |
| `creator` | `.claude/skills/great-tables-creator/` | A/B candidate, mounted as `great-tables` | Evaluating alternative skill designs. |
| *baseline* | *(no `.claude/` at all)*              | The model has no skill guidance | Control for lift measurement. |

Every variant produces the same on-disk shape: one `table.py`, one
`table.png`, one `transcript.json`. The runner's `--skill` flag picks
which of the four gets mounted; see the
[runner reference](runner.qmd#-skill-proseshcriptscreatorhouse--defaults-prose).

## `great-tables` (prose)

The default. A **flowchart, not a menu**: for most decisions there is
one deterministic rule (or one explicit, data-driven branch). The
`SKILL.md` carries only the procedure and decision points; every pinned
value — palette hex codes, band rules, API signatures, polish checklists
— lives in a `references/` file that `references/REFERENCE.md` routes to.

Loading pattern:

1. Read `references/REFERENCE.md` before writing any Python.
2. Follow the 7-step flowchart: understand data → organize columns →
   Big Color (which measures earn fill) → heading band → Small-Color
   checklist → titles/annotations → render + verify.
3. Render with `gt.gtsave("table.png")` — the mandatory renderer.

Pick this when you want the highest-polish output and don't mind the
larger reference-tree footprint in-context.

## `great-tables-ci` (scripts)

Same flowchart as the prose skill, but ships a **checker loop** and two
executable scripts under `scripts/`:

- `gt_check.py` — inspects a generated `table.py` for common
  correctness/style violations (hairline visibility, palette
  consistency, formatter selection).
- `gt_consistency.py` — a small library the agent's own script can
  import to enforce house-style choices.

The `references/` and `assets/` trees are symlinks back to the prose
skill's copies (single source of truth); `_prepare_skill_root()` calls
`copytree(symlinks=False)` so the ephemeral mount materializes the
resolved files.

Pick this when you want the model to self-check its output before
declaring done.

## `great-tables-house` (thin house-style)

The **minimal path**. No flowchart, no archetype directory, no reference
router. Instead:

1. One worked script: `scripts/house_table.py`. Reads as both the
   canonical example (run it directly to see the reference render) and
   a helper module exposing `PALETTE`, `frame()`, `finalize()`,
   `band()`, `stripe()`, `stub_tint()`, `heatmap()`, `status_chip()`,
   `summary_row()`, `group_emphasis()`, `humanize_labels()`.
2. One short rules file: `references/data.md` — answers three
   questions the flowchart skills handle with dedicated steps (what
   identifies a row, what a named-but-not-literal measure computes to,
   how to tie-break unranked measures).

Pick this when the request looks simple (a plain list, one or two
numeric columns) but the house style still applies.

## `great-tables-creator` (candidate)

A **candidate skill** produced by the skill-creator workflow. Its
frontmatter declares `name: great-tables`, so when the runner mounts
it, the ephemeral `.claude/skills/great-tables/` looks identical to
what the prose skill would produce — same skill name, same trigger
conditions, different internals.

This is what the harness uses to A/B a candidate skill design against
the promoted prose skill. Run the same corpus under `--skill prose` and
`--skill creator`, compare the two `summary.json` files (or the two
`comparator_score.png` plots), decide whether the candidate wins.

Pick this only when you're evaluating an alternative skill design. It
is not intended for production table generation.

## The baseline (no-skill control)

`--baseline` (or `--repeat N` with `N > 1`, which auto-enables it) runs
one invocation per prompt with `variant="none"`. The agent sees no
`.claude/` at all — no skill, no `settings.local.json` — and is
launched with `skills=[]`. It has full access to `great_tables` at
runtime; what it lacks is any of the skill's guidance about *how* to
use it.

The baseline is the control that lets the harness compute **lift**: how
much better the with-skill table scores than the same prompt run
without it.

## Picking a skill

- **Just want a good table?** → `prose`.
- **Want the model to self-check?** → `scripts`.
- **Simplest request, want minimal context spend?** → `house`.
- **A/B evaluating an alternative skill?** → `creator` vs. `prose`.
- **Need to measure how much the skill actually helps?** →
  `--repeat 3` (any variant); the auto-baseline gives you the control.
